proposition: Under the map n -> n/2 when n is even, n -> 3n+1 when n is odd, every integer n with 1 <= n <= 200000 reaches 1 in fewer than 340 steps.
hypotheses: the stopping time counts steps until the value 1 is reached

argument.text: Every n in [1, 50] has stopping time below 340; the smallest values are checked directly.
A direct sweep verifies that every n in [1, 5000] has stopping time below 340.
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 2000].
There exists an integer n in [1, 2000] with n^2 > 2000.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 2000 we have n^2 >= 2n.
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 5.
The sweep covers [1, 5000]; the statement is asserted for every n in [1, 200000].
